title: Platform systems & services: runbooks, dashboards, alerts, roadmap (Q2 2026)
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:

This page centralizes Platform Engineering (Platform Systems & Services) guidance: service ownership, how-tos, dashboard and alert standards, canonical runbooks, recent retrospectives, and the near-term roadmap (Q2 2026). Use this as the single-entry index for operational procedures and links to team wiki pages.

Owner & contact:
- Team: Platform (eng-platform)
- Primary oncall contact: platform-oncall@redwood.com
- Doc owner: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.com)

Scope:
- Core systems: service discovery, ingress & API gateway, routing layer, shared caches, metrics & tracing, CI/CD for infra, and internal platform services (auth-proxy, feature-flags, secrets-manager).
- Deliverables: approved runbooks, dashboard templates, alerting playbooks, ownership matrix, and quarterly roadmap items.

Table of contents:
1. Systems & services inventory
2. How-tos (common tasks)
3. Dashboards & alerts (standards + templates)
4. Runbooks (incident & maintenance)
5. Retrospective: Incident P-1 2026-05-13 (summary + actions)
6. Roadmap: Q2 2026 priorities
7. Team wiki & knowledge transfer

1) Systems & services inventory
- Auth-proxy: internal auth/gateway used by Dedicated and Private deployments (owner: infra-auth)
- Platform Router (plat-router): routes tenant traffic to model-serving clusters, exposes health, metrics (owner: serving-router)
- KV Cache (plat-kv): Redis-backed prefix cache for prefix/KV caching with smart eviction (owner: caching-team)
- Observability pipeline: Prometheus -> Cortex -> Grafana + Tempo tracing (owner: observability)
- Secrets-manager: tenant KMS bridge (owner: security-infra)
- CI/CD infra: fleet pipelines and canary deploy system (owner: ci-platform)

Service ownership matrix:
| Service | Owner team | Pager | SLO |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| plat-router | serving-router | platform-pager | 99.95% availability, p99 latency < 45ms for control-plane calls |
| plat-kv | caching-team | platform-pager | 99.9% availability, median get < 6ms |
| observability | observability | observability-pager | Metrics ingestion 24h window, query 95th perc < 200ms |

2) How-tos (common tasks)
- How to onboard a new service to platform monitoring:
  1. Add Prometheus scrape config: /etc/prometheus/scrape.d/<service>.yaml (example below)
  2. Instrument runtime metrics (go/prom client) and expose /metrics and /healthz endpoints
  3. Create Grafana dashboard from the dashboard template (see section 3)
  4. Add alert rules to cortex-alerts repo and request review

Scrape config example (yaml):
---
- job_name: 'service-PLAT-EXAMPLE'
  static_configs:
    - targets: ['10.10.12.34:9100']
  relabel_configs:
    - source_labels: [__address__]
      target_label: instance
---

- How to add a new alert (summary):
  1. Open a PR on cortex-alerts (alerts/rules/<service>.yaml) with description and runbook link
  2. Ensure the alert includes: severity, runbook URL, owner tag, and a long/short form
  3. Request two reviewers from observability and the service owner

3) Dashboards & alerts (standards + templates)
Standards summary:
- Dashboards must use the platform dashboard template and include: Overview, Latency, Errors, Traffic, Resource (CPU/GPU) utilization, and Important logs snippet panel.
- Service overview row should be visible at 1366x768 and load within 1.5s.
- Alert severities: Sev1 (P0/P1) = page immediately, Sev2 (P2) = notify oncall w/ 15m SLA, Sev3 = ticketed.

Canonical alert thresholds (examples):
- Control-plane p50 latency > 200ms for 5m -> Sev2
- Control-plane p99 latency > 1s for 3m -> Sev1
- Error rate (5xx) > 1% of requests for 5m -> Sev1
- Prometheus scrape failures > 3 targets down for 10m -> Sev2

Dashboard template checklist:
- Panels: 1) Requests/sec, 2) p50/p95/p99 latency, 3) 5xx errors and error rate, 4) resource usage per node, 5) request distribution by route, 6) recent logs (last 5m)
- Annotations: deploy events and schema-rollouts pulled from CI/CD tags
- Links: runbook URL, ownership, incident-history link

4) Runbooks (incident & maintenance)
Canonical incident runbook (short):
1. Triage (0-10m): Confirm impact, map affected services, set incident severity and timeline, notify oncall and execs if Sev1.
2. Mitigate (10-60m): If possible, enable automatic fallbacks (route to secondary region/model-variant), scale up Dedicated pools, or apply circuit-breaker to degrade non-critical routes.
3. Remediate (60m+): Apply code rollback, configuration fix, or infrastructure patch. Coordinate with CI/CD for canary then full rollout.
4. Post-incident (within 72h): Draft postmortem, include timeline, root cause, and remediation steps. Assign action items and owners.

Planned maintenance playbook (short):
1. Schedule in calendar + status page update (at least 48h notice)
2. Run pre-checks: health, canaries, backups, and rollback plan
3. Execute during low-traffic window and monitor key dashboards
4. Validate and close maintenance ticket; update runbook if any surprises

5) Retrospective: P-1 incident 2026-05-13 (summary)
Summary:
- Impact: Intermittent control-plane timeouts across plat-router and plat-kv during peak model rollouts. Customer-facing latency increased; several Dedicated customers observed degraded throughput. Incident lasted ~2.5 hours with automated fallbacks triggering for most tenants.
- Root cause: Race condition in plat-router connection pool combined with a degraded Redis instance that increased KV latency; under heavy rollout traffic the router hit p99 backpressure thresholds and tripped circuit-breakers.

Action items (status):
1. Fix connection pool race condition (owner: serving-router) — completed 2026-06-01
2. Harden Redis monitoring + autoscaling (owner: caching-team) — in progress (ETA 2026-07-30)
3. Add integration test for model-rollout + cache-throttle (owner: platform-qa) — in progress (ETA 2026-07-15)
4. Improve dashboard for coordinated health of router + cache (owner: observability) — completed 2026-06-20

Lessons learned:
- System-level chaos testing for combined router+cache workloads was missing; add to quarterly game-day plan.
- Ensure runbooks include explicit fallback rollout toggles and customer-communication templates.

6) Roadmap: Q2 2026 priorities (summary)
- Stability & SLOs (Q2-Q3): end-to-end SLA observability for control-plane latency and KV caching, targeted p99 reduction of 30% by end of Q3.
- Platform autoscaling v2 (Q2 2026): improved node-level autoscaler with GPU-aware bin-packing and predictive scaling by traffic patterns (owner: ci-platform, infra-sre).
- Observability improvements (Q2 2026): faster dashboard templates, synthetic telemetry for canaries, and improved alert deduplication (owner: observability).
- Runbook & GT templates (Q2 2026): standardize incident comms and customer-impact notices for Dedicated customers (owner: platform).

Milestones (next 90 days):
- 2026-07-01: Autobump router connection-pool patch to canary clusters
- 2026-07-15: Integration test coverage for rollout+cache scenarios
- 2026-08-01: Autoscaling v2 alpha deploy to test fleet
